source_document.body:
Orient Overseas Container Line reported a 45.1% year-over-year increase in third-quarter liner revenue to $3.28 billion, as higher revenue per container and increased cargo volumes drove gains across all four of its reported trade regions.
OOCL handled 2.12 million twenty-foot equivalent units in the quarter ended Sept. 30, up 9% from a year earlier, according to an Oct. 9 operational update from parent Orient Overseas (International) Ltd., itself majority-owned by China’s Cosco Shipping Holdings . Average liner revenue per TEU increased 33.1%.
Cargo growth outpaced a 3.6% increase in loadable capacity. OOIL reported that the overall load factor increased 4.2% compared with the third quarter of 2025.
Trans-Pacific leads revenue growth
The trans-Pacific trade delivered the largest revenue increase among OOCL’s reported regions. Revenue rose 71.8% to $1.44 billion, while container volumes increased 13.1% to 595,139 TEUs. That compared with revenue of $837.9 million and volumes of 526,032 TEUs in the same quarter last year.
Asia-Europe recorded the fastest volume growth, with liftings rising 15.4% to 399,162 TEUs. Revenue on the trade increased 45% to $695.8 million.
Intra-Asia and Australasia remained OOCL’s largest region by container volume, handling 981,336 TEUs, up 4.6%. Revenue increased 23.7% to $947.6 million. Trans-Atlantic volumes rose 7.3% to 147,008 TEUs, while revenue increased 11.9% to $201.8 million.
Revenue growth exceeded volume growth in each region, consistent with the company’s reported increase in average revenue per TEU . The update did not identify the market conditions behind those gains.
Nine-month revenue approaches $8 billion
For the first nine months of 2026, OOCL’s liner revenue increased 18.9% to $7.96 billion from $6.70 billion a year earlier. Container volumes rose 6.5% to 6.25 million TEUs, while average liner revenue per TEU increased 11.6%.
Loadable capacity increased 4.8% over the nine-month period, and OOIL reported a 1.4% increase in the overall load factor. Trans-Pacific revenue rose 27% to $3.16 billion, while Asia-Europe revenue increased 19% to $1.70 billion. Intra-Asia and Australasia revenue grew 13.8% to $2.55 billion, and trans-Atlantic revenue edged up 2.2% to $556.3 million.
The operational update did not include earnings or expense figures.
